gen-comfortaa-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Round, bright, tube-bent letters up top. Comfortaa earns its place on big, short headings, while Noto Sans NKo Unjoined follows below with wide openings on its small letters.
gen-comfortaa-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Noto Sans Shavian runs loose, with curves that never knot at the ends. Comfortaa above it has no calligraphic shading at all, just smooth uniform strokes, so give the Shavian text a little extra size to hold its own.
gen-comfortaa-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-n: Noto Znamenny Musical Notation lets its terminals stop well away from the stem, giving each letter breathing space. Comfortaa answers with crossbars as heavy as its stems, so the page feels drawn by two different hands.
gen-comfortaa-gf-ojuju: A wide ring for a c, and every stroke drawn like neon tubing: that is Comfortaa. Ojuju then comes in with the mild contrast of a lightly flexed spring wire, giving the text a gentler, more varied line.
gen-comfortaa-gf-overpass: Comfortaa stretches its spacing like an uncoiled spring, and its c is a nearly closed ring of glowing tube. Overpass stays crisp underneath, so a slightly larger size for it is worth a look.
gen-comfortaa-gf-palanquin: Palanquin builds its curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths that let the text breathe. But Comfortaa squeezes its strokes out like toothpaste in one steady line, so the heading looks rounder and more uniform than the body.
gen-comfortaa-gf-philosopher: Comfortaa draws everything at a single weight, with a flat, stencil-cut feel and a ring-shaped c. Philosopher below swells and thins softly, so the text has a gentle ebb and flow.
gen-comfortaa-gf-pontano-sans: Soft rings, stretched spacing. Comfortaa draws its bowls and stems at the same weight, while Pontano Sans keeps its c terminals wide open underneath, so the heading looks sculpted and the text looks easygoing.
gen-comfortaa-gf-quattrocento-sans: Comfortaa builds every letter on a monoweight skeleton, like neon tube. Quattrocento Sans keeps clear gaps so its c never collapses into an o, which makes a longer passage feel open and unhurried.
gen-comfortaa-gf-red-hat-text: Red Hat Text reads crisp, with the line weight of a technical drawing pen and curvy, unclamped letters. Comfortaa is the one for a bright, ring-shaped c in a heading, while Red Hat Text handles the steady running text.
